objective: Exploratory census under a frozen contract on PROCESS-CHAIN-20261108-001B's chains and its stress-test chains: per chain, the cycle lags at which c2 binds the end rings, depends on both end rings, and both contacts bind; decide three frozen hypotheses: arrival (composition exactly at the lags where the far ring's influence arrives), coexistence (both contacts bind at every composing lag), and transport (a rule and law that compose at recurring lags at one size do so at every declared size).
status: Closed: supported 2026-11-08 (exploratory): of 7,040 chains, 244 compose at recurring lags; H1 (composing = arrival lags), H2 (both contacts bind there) and H3 (transport across sizes) all fail as universal statements, but in 92 chains, every one with an affine rule (15, 170, 60, 90, 105, 150), the composing lags are singled out by the chain; never with a nonlinear rule; 20 rule-law groups compose at every decided size. Control passed.
title: Are the composing lags native?
